newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WGC says Russia bought 127 tonnes of gold in 1996.
newsitem.headline: WGC says Russia bought 127 tonnes of gold in 1996.

text.p: The World Gold Council (WGC) said on Tuesday that 127 tonnes of gold purchased by Russia's central bank was made over calendar 1996.
George Milling-Stanley, WGC manager of gold analysis, said the figure was based on new data from the International Monetary Fund, but gave no other details.
The fact a central bank was seen to be a buyer of gold was good news for gold, George Milling-Stanley, earlier told the Diggers and Dealers mining conference in this Australian gold mining centre.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) contributed to a fall in the gold price to a 12-year low earlier this month after it announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold, two-thirds of its gold reserves, over the past six months.
Milling-Stanley is scheduled to hold a news conference later on Tuesday.
